newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia July-April budget deficit A$8.933 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australia July-April budget deficit A$8.933 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the 10 months to April, the first 10 months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$8.933 billion, compared with A$12.251 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Monday.
The headline balance -- which includes asset sales -- was a A$4.657 billion deficit, compared with a A$7.716 billion deficit for the same period last fiscal year, Fahey said in a statement.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Revenue growth to April was 7.8 percent, compared with the 6.5 percent growth that underpins the A$6.9 billion 1996/97 deficit estimate published in the May 13 budget.
Underlying outlays grew 3.9 percent, compared with the budget projection of 3.4 percent, Fahey said.
Revenue growth was fuelled by a 7.8 percent increase in tax receipts over the same period in 1995/96.
The main increases in spending were social security and welfare, and lower state government debt repayments.

The monthly headline balance for April was a A$513 million surplus, compared with a surplus of A$607 million a year earlier. The underlying balance for the month was a $230 million surplus, compared with a A$1.016 billion surplus in April 1996.
